bigFiveItems.text: I see myself as someone who is reserved.
I see myself as someone who is generally trusting.
I see myself as someone who tends to be lazy.
I see myself as someone who is relaxed, handles stress well.
I see myself as someone who has few artistic interests.
I see myself as someone who is outgoing, sociable.
I see myself as someone who tends to find fault with others.
I see myself as someone who does a thorough job.
I see myself as someone who gets nervous easily.
I see myself as someone who has an active imagination.

gunaItems.text: If you are working on a project that looks like it will fail, do you continue to put in your best effort until the very end?
How much time per week do you spend voluntarily learning something new (reading, watching documentaries) just for the sake of understanding?
If taking a shortcut (like skipping a queue or bending a regulation) would guarantee you a major win, how likely are you to take it?
When solving a problem, how often do you dismiss traditional or old-fashioned approaches in favor of your own logic?
How often do you check your social media likes or exam grades and feel a sudden rush of pride or superiority?
After achieving a goal, how quickly do you feel restless and start chasing the next achievement?
How often do you put off important tasks until the last minute, even when you know it will stress you out?
When faced with a complex problem, how often do you freeze up and wait for someone else to solve it for you?
Do you frequently look at your life and feel 'stuck' or like you are 'falling behind' everyone else?
If a gym workout or a study session gets difficult, how likely are you to quit early and tell yourself 'I'll do it tomorrow'?
How many New Year's resolutions or self-improvement plans have you started and dropped within 2 weeks?
On Sunday evening, do you feel a knot in your stomach thinking about work/school on Monday?
If an elderly family member gives you advice that contradicts your own plans, how likely are you to listen respectfully and seriously consider their perspective?
In a heated argument, how much effort do you make to keep your tone calm and avoid using harsh words?
If you promise to help a friend move house, but wake up feeling tired and lazy, how likely are you to go anyway simply because you gave your word?
How often do you treat the campus janitor/security guard with the exact same respect and patience as you do your Professor or Dean?
If a friend invites you to a lecture on philosophy or spirituality, how likely are you to decline because you find it 'boring' or 'useless'?
How often do you find yourself admiring or following rich influencers and celebrities rather than scientists or social workers?
If someone asks for a donation, do you feel annoyed or resentful, even if you eventually give a small amount?
When things go wrong in your life, how often do you feel that it was completely someone else's fault at 'the world is against you'?
In your head or with friends, how often do you find yourself making fun of or judging strangers/acquaintances?
How many times a week do you feel a flash of rage (at traffic, people, or technology)?
Do you feel like you are always the one giving in relationships while others just take from you?
When talking to friends, how often do you find yourself mostly complaining about your problems?
When a friend succeeds (gets a job/promotion), how often do you feel a pang of jealousy or 'Why not me?'
I often neglect my responsibilities to my friends
How often do you act aggressively or violently towards others when upset?
When given a choice at a buffet, how often do you naturally gravitate towards fresh fruits and salads over heavy or spicy dishes?
If a cashier gives you too much change, how likely are you to immediately point out the mistake and return the money?
To what extent do you live your life with the assumption that this physical existence is the only reality that matters?
How much do you crave spicy, salty, or very rich foods (like fried snacks or heavy desserts) compared to plain, simple meals?
If you lost your phone or favorite watch today, how strictly would it affect your mood and sense of self-worth for the next week?
On a free evening, how often do you choose loud social outings (parties, clubs) over quiet, solitary activities?
How much of your daily mental energy is spent thinking about or pursuing romantic/sexual gratification?
When looking at a buffet or a sale, do you often take more than you actually need, just because it's available?
After buying something you really wanted, how quickly do you start wanting a better version of it?
How often do you feel you could be genuinely happy living in a simple house without luxury items?
How frequently do you prioritize physical enjoyment (like food, comfort, or sex) over your other responsibilities?
How often do you do something impulsive (like staying up late or skipping work) and regret it the next morning?
How often do you struggle to get out of bed because the day ahead feels pointless or too heavy?
If you could get away with not paying a bus fare or sneaking into a movie, would you do it?
If there is a box of cookies in front of you and you decided not to eat one, how long can you resist before giving in?
How often do you find yourself wishing you could escape to a quiet village rather than living in the busy city?
How often do you feel controlled by a physical or psychological habit/addiction that you can't break?
When you look at an animal or another person, to what extent do you feel a deep, underlying connection or shared 'life force' with them?
When facing a difficult decision where you could gain personally by bending the rules, how often do you stop to ask yourself 'Is this the right thing to do?'
Imagine you made a mistake at work/school that no one else noticed. How likely are you to admit it voluntarily?
Think about a time when you had nothing to do and no entertainment. How comfortable/happy were you just 'being' with yourself?
Before taking action, how often do you consult higher ethical or moral principles?
How often do you feel that 'self-realization' or 'spiritual growth' is irrelevant to your real-life goals?
On a typical day, what percentage of the time do you feel a general sense of 'blah' or dissatisfaction for no specific reason?
If you miss a bus or drop your coffee, does it ruin your entire morning?
Do you often feel a vague sense of dread or anxiety about the future without knowing exactly why?
Do your moods swing wildly during the day (e.g., fine one minute, crying/angry the next)?
How often do you feel 'down in the dumps' or 'low energy' even when nothing bad has happened?
Do you often 'forget' or avoid doing chores/errands that your family asked you to do?
I often feel mentally unbalanced or chaotic inside
